name: Harpy
description: The Harpies are winged spirits in Greek mythology, originally personifications of stormy winds and divine snatchers. They appear in early sources as fair-haired winged maidens and in later literature as bird-bodied, women-faced monsters who steal food and abduct people as agents of divine punishment.

aliases.name: Aello
aliases.meaning: 'Storm-swift' — an individual harpy named in Hesiod

aliases.name: Ocypete
aliases.meaning: 'Swift-wing' — an individual harpy named in Hesiod

aliases.name: Celaeno
aliases.meaning: 'Dark, dusky' — an individual harpy added by Virgil

aliases.name: Podarge
aliases.meaning: 'Fleet-foot' — a harpy named in Homer; mother of Achilles' horses Balius and Xanthus

origin: Mythologically, the wider Greek and Mediterranean world: Thrace (Phineus), the Strophades (Aeneid), the cave of Zephyrus, and stormy maritime regions in general. Culturally, harpies have been received throughout the Greco-Roman, medieval European, and modern global imaginary.
